# Peas API: start with a task

Import the public package once:

```zig
const std = @import("std");
const up = @import("unpolished-peas");
```

Start with [installation](../guides/installation.md) and the
[compiled quickstart](../guides/quickstart.md) for an independent project.
Use this reference when you need a call, its options, or its cleanup rule.

| I want to… | Reference | Complete recipe / guide |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Write a game with init, fixed update and draw | [Lifecycle and GameContext](lifecycle.md) | [Game protocol](../guides/game-protocol.md) |
| Draw shapes, text or an offscreen surface | [Canvas and RenderSurface](drawing.md) | [Rendering](../guides/rendering.md), [surfaces](../guides/render-surfaces.md) |
| Read keys, rebind controls or enter a Unicode name | [Input and text](input.md) | [Input workbench](../../examples/input_workbench_game.zig), [input guide](../guides/input.md) |
| Load an image/font/sheet with one cleanup | [Assets and animation](assets.md) | [Compiled asset recipes](../guides/asset-recipes.md) |
| Play effects or music, save progress | [Audio and saves](audio-save.md) | [Sound](../guides/audio-assets.md), [save bytes](../guides/save-data.md) |
| Reproduce a bug without a window | [Headless and replay](testing.md) | [Testing](../guides/testing.md), [downstream conformance](../guides/portable-conformance.md) |
| Use files, an SDL window, or GPU effects | [Host and advanced boundaries](boundaries.md) | [Core contract](../guides/core-contract.md), [advanced 2D](../guides/advanced-2d.md) |

## Reading the reference

Each topic combines ownership/error guidance with source-derived declarations,
member links, field defaults, and examples extracted from executed Zig sources.
The signatures retain implementation-local names: for example,
`Map` in an ActionMap signature means `up.input.ActionMap`, and `Self`
means the containing type (or the type returned by a generic factory).
The source link resolves other local aliases; import through the public
`up` path shown in each heading. A declaration block is a reference excerpt,
not a complete standalone Zig file.

Struct field listings describe storage and defaults. Prefer the documented
operations; replacing an owner's allocator/buffers or deinitializing a
borrowed field can violate its lifetime even when Zig permits field access.

Examples use `std = @import("std")` and up as above. Each excerpt links to
the full compiled module and identifies whether it is a function, game type or
test. Tests need a test build; SDL entry points belong only in native wrappers.
The small [reference recipes](../../examples/api_reference_recipes.zig) run
natively and in freestanding Wasm. The existing asset and input workbenches
exercise the fuller native/browser workflows.

## Portability and support

The ordinary portable path is GameContext + Input + CPU Canvas, embedded
assets, optional host audio/save capabilities and explicit game ownership.
The core contract does not make every helper in a namespace portable:
filesystem helpers are native-only; replay recording under
`preview.developer` is preview developer tooling; Renderer2D has a separate
advanced contract. Browser renderer support remains subject to the
[capability matrix](../guides/capabilities.md).

These pages cover common game-authoring APIs, not every inspector, profiler,
mixer, backend, or packaging helper. See [boundaries](boundaries.md) for those
entry points. This reference neither expands the stable API nor changes
existing compatibility guarantees.

## Maintenance

In the engine checkout, run `zig build docs-update-api -Dwith_sdl=false` after changing a referenced
declaration, example or template, and review the generated diff in docs/api.
`zig build docs test-docs -Dwith_sdl=false` emits the site in zig-out/docs
and rejects stale reference pages, broken local/member links and unresolved
public paths. `test-docs` also runs the native and Wasm recipe checks and
requires Node.js 24. Generation itself needs only Zig 0.15.2.
Edit templates in docs/api/templates; generated pages are checked in so links
work while browsing the repository. Signatures/defaults and excerpts follow
source automatically; ownership/error prose still needs human review.
Member fragments preserve Zig's case: Input.Snapshot and Input.snapshot have
distinct anchors.

The emitted Markdown includes linked guides, fixtures and source/example
snapshots under `repository/`. Links are rewritten and checked in that output
tree, so it can be moved for browsing. Source snapshots are reading material,
not an independent game package; use the original examples and installation
workflow to build a game.
